sentences.text: 1 2. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that relations between the victim and the petitioner were consensual; no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused- petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. I have considered the submissions made by both the parties and perused the material available on record.
5. Perusal of the material revealing that the victim is a married lady and having two kids.

As per her,
she came into contact with the petitioner a year prior from the date of lodging of the FIR.

There is substance that the relation between the petitioner and the victim were consensual since it is noticed that they used to establish physical relationship on several occasions but on the pretext that she was threatened by the petitioner, seems to be a disputed fact as the same could be ascertained by the learned trial Court after taking entire evidence on record.
There is a delay of one year and further three months after having latest cause of action for reporting the matter to the police for which no satisfactory explanation has been furnished by her.
Be that as it may, I see no reason to allow further incarceration of the [2024:RJ-JD:12588] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-3043/2024] petitioner.
Thus, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
6. It is nigh well settled that at a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction so that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.
Otherwise, it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

7. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARJAND ALI),J 34-MAMTA/-
